welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.lead: The app sorts your Ableton projects into songs, tells you which ones open, and repairs the ones that can be.
welcome.copyBeside: A repair writes a copy next to the project.
welcome.time: Setup takes two minutes, plus the time of the first scan.
welcome.noLive: Ableton Live doesn't seem to have been opened on this computer: without its plugin list, the app can't tell what is missing. Open Live once, then come back here (or carry on, the scan will run again by itself).

projects.title: Where are your projects?
projects.lead: Choose the folder or folders that hold your Ableton projects (the .als files). Subfolders are read too, however you organise them: one folder per song, or everything in a single folder.

samples.title: Your samples
samples.lead: When a project can no longer find a sample, the app looks for it elsewhere. It already looks in your projects folders and Ableton's library. Add the other folders where you keep sounds: packs, banks, an old drive.
samples.midiHint: The MIDI files in your projects and samples folders are already read. Only add a folder here if there are more elsewhere (construction kits, packs): the app only reads the MIDI files in it.

scan.lead: Each project is read once. After that, only what changes is read again. You can leave the window open.
scan.none: No projects found in these folders. Go back to choose others.
scan.midiPhase: Your projects are ready. MIDI files are still being read in the background (the sidebar shows the progress): you can carry on and explore the app meanwhile.
scan.cancelled: Scan stopped: what was read is kept, the rest will be read at the next scan.

artists.title: Your artists
artists.lead: If you produce under several names (aliases, groups, collaborations), the app files each song under the right one.
artists.leadGiven: The name given at the Projects step is already there.
artists.leadFound: Here are also the names found in your folders and files: untick what isn't an artist.
artists.noneFound: No other names found in the folders.
artists.oldWindows: An old Windows on another drive (dual boot)?
artists.oldWindowsHint: Its plugins and samples help repair old projects.
